reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is a tutorial about enabling Flash in Chrome and Microsoft Edge using browser settings. The Patreon mention and social media links are presented as creator support or audience connection requests, without a deceptive benefit, required payment, investment return, or credential request.

there's flash and it says ask first . So I'm gonna click on that and I'm going to change it from ask first to simply allow sites to run flash
Now let's take a look at Microsoft Edge

opening.argument: The video repeatedly directs viewers toward actions that benefit the presenter: supporting the creator on Patreon, connecting through social-media accounts, clicking Like, and subscribing. The tutorial supplies a low-effort pathway from viewing to external engagement, while the audience is not given a clear account of what it receives in return. That combination can function as a low-barrier acquisition funnel even though the promised benefit is left implicit. The browser instructions make the request appear practical and trustworthy, but they do not explain why viewers should extend support or follow the listed links.

citations.quote: Consider supporting Technology for Teachers and Students on Patreon
please click the LIKE button, and definitely do subscribe to this YouTube channel
please consider connecting with me on my social media websites

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the Patreon mention ordinary creator support does not eliminate the solicitation. The video also asks viewers to Like, subscribe, and connect through several outside channels, so the practical tutorial doubles as a conversion point. The defense identifies what the presenter requests, but does not establish that the audience receives any concrete value for taking those actions. The absence of an explicit payoff is compatible with an intentionally vague low-barrier acquisition pitch.

citations.quote: Consider supporting Technology for Teachers and Students on Patreon
please click the LIKE button, and definitely do subscribe to this YouTube channel

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These requests do not establish the required promise-action relationship. The Patreon text asks for support, while the closing asks for ordinary audience engagement; neither promises cash, an asset, a return, or a withdrawal. The tutorial's actual subject is browser configuration, including Flash permissions, and the cited requests do not transform that instruction into a scam.

citations.quote: In this short tutorial, learn how to enable flash in the Google Chrome browser as well as the Microsoft Edge browser.
if this video has been useful, please click the LIKE button, and definitely do subscribe to this YouTube channel

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an external Patreon destination, multiple social-media destinations, shortened links visible in the social-media panel, and repeated requests to follow, Like, and subscribe. Those channels move the audience away from the browser demonstration and toward actions controlled by the presenter. The video does not explain the terms, benefits, or safeguards associated with those destinations. A careful judge should therefore treat the apparently harmless tutorial as an unusually broad external-engagement funnel, with the requested actions easier to verify than any benefit offered to viewers.

citations.quote: https://www.patreon.com/technologyforteachersandstudents
please consider connecting with me on my social media websites, like Facebook, Pinterest, and Twitter
please click the LIKE button, and definitely do subscribe to this YouTube channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the browser settings and treats the external destinations as incidental, but the closing expressly promotes social accounts and channel engagement. The social panel displays several destinations, including shortened addresses, while the Patreon URL is supplied separately. This concentration of off-platform pathways is a genuine risk signal even without a stated monetary return, because the viewer is encouraged to continue beyond the demonstrated settings.

citations.quote: https://www.patreon.com/technologyforteachersandstudents
please consider connecting with me on my social media websites, like Facebook, Pinterest, and Twitter

true_side_reply.rebuttal: External links and social accounts are not themselves evidence of a scam. The supplied material identifies the Patreon destination as creator support and does not promise a reward, return, asset, or withdrawal for visiting it. The frame shows social-media destinations, but it does not show deceptive claims or a payment flow. Risk signals cannot substitute for the missing promise-action relationship.

citations.quote: Consider supporting Technology for Teachers and Students on Patreon

opening.argument: Although presented as technical education, the video uses the instructional role to establish credibility before steering viewers toward promotion. It ends with requests to connect on several social platforms, Like the video, subscribe to the channel, and anticipate recurring uploads. The tutorial framing can therefore be understood as promotional packaging for audience acquisition rather than a purely informational service. The browser steps provide useful context, but they also make the surrounding solicitation appear more trustworthy without supplying a specific viewer benefit.

citations.quote: In this short movie tutorial I am going to show you how to enable flash in various browsers
please consider connecting with me on my social media websites, like Facebook, Pinterest, and Twitter
please click the LIKE button, and definitely do subscribe to this YouTube channel
you can look forward to another video at least every Monday

rebuttal.rebuttal: The technical subject does not neutralize the promotional structure. After presenting browser instructions, the speaker asks for several forms of audience participation and advertises continued publication. That sequencing turns education into a trust-building wrapper for channel growth and external attention. The defense says there is no deceptive benefit, but promotional steering can be the operative mechanism even when the payoff is not stated plainly.

citations.quote: please consider connecting with me on my social media websites, like Facebook, Pinterest, and Twitter
you can look forward to another video at least every Monday

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional role is supported by the video's substantive content: it explains how to enable Flash in multiple browsers and how to manage website permissions. A request for Likes, subscriptions, or social follows is normal channel promotion, not evidence that viewers are promised an asset or financial return. The argument reframes ordinary audience-building but identifies no false claim, payment demand, or deceptive outcome.
